title: Employees Earning More Than Their Managers
description:
Write an SQL query to find the employees who earn more than their managers.

Table `Employee`: `id (INT), name (TEXT), salary (INT), managerId (INT)`
output_format: Names of employees earning more than their manager.
constraints: managerId references id in the same table.

sample_tests.input:
CREATE TABLE Employee (id INT, name TEXT, salary INT, managerId INT);
INSERT INTO Employee VALUES (1, 'Joe', 70000, 3), (2, 'Henry', 80000, 4), (3, 'Sam', 60000, NULL), (4, 'Max', 90000, NULL);
sample_tests.explanation: Joe earns 70,000, which is more than his manager Sam (60,000).

hidden_tests.input:
CREATE TABLE Employee (id INT, name TEXT, salary INT, managerId INT);
INSERT INTO Employee VALUES (1, 'A', 50000, 2), (2, 'B', 40000, NULL);

hints: Self-join `Employee` with itself aliased as `e` (employee) and `m` (manager).

reference_solution: SELECT e.name FROM Employee e JOIN Employee m ON e.managerId = m.id WHERE e.salary > m.salary;
